chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Photographs from Korea: Pruitt and Bernie Peacock
summary: Describing a 1952 Korea photo and trouble with Carl Pruitt and Bernie Peacock.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I PUT IT DOWN, I MENTIONED IT ON THE CASSETTE SO IT'S ON THERE. THEY DON'T NEED IT. THAT'S THE ONE. NOW THIS IS IN KOREA. 1952 in Korea.
THIS IS GALBRAITH, KENNY BRIAN, WILLARD BROWN, I CAN'T SEE THE DRUMMER. SNUBBY AND IS THIS PRUITT AGAIN? WHY DID YOU HAVE HIM.
I don't know, he was recommended to me I was so (inaudible) I had to send him back.
WHO DID YOU USED TO HAVE.
Everybody had trouble with him. But Benny Goodman had him for a while.
HE DIDN'T LAS LONG WITH BENNY.
He didn't last long with Benny.
WHERE DID YOU GET BERNIE PEACOCK FROM TO BEGIN WITH?
I don't remember where I got Bernie Peacock from,
but I know I wish I had him.
The funny thing about him was I remember meeting him that time he sent me a record, he moved back to Detroit, it's where his home is.
This over in a hospital in Korea.
Huey was up in the Sierras, but he just wasn't, he was outing somewhere. Yeah, Huey Long was on this trip. This is the same band.
That's Jack McVay, he gave a party for me when I came back from overseas. This is Marcia Mayer, she was from Oklahoma.
